reason: The text portrays Yahweh as actively supporting the Hebrew people (Israel) against their enemies. David explicitly invokes Yahweh's past deliverance (from lion and bear) and future protection. Saul tells David 'Go, and may the Lord be with you.' Most significantly, David proclaims that 'the Lord will deliver you [the Philistine] into my hand' and 'the battle is the Lord's, and he will give you into our hands,' clearly positioning Yahweh as allied with Israel against the Philistine adversary. The entire narrative demonstrates Yahweh's favor toward the Israelite people.
